instruction: Insert a page break before the 'Conclusion' section in this document and save it.

command: import pyautogui, time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(1); pyautogui.press('enter'); time.sleep(1)

llm_judge_reasons: The getter now correctly locates the 'Conclusion' paragraph via case-insensitive text matching and checks whether a page break appears immediately before it.

Check 1 (pageBreakBefore property on the Conclusion paragraph) and Check 2 (explicit w:br[@w:type='page'] run in preceding paragraphs) together cover all common ways a user can insert a page break before a section in LibreOffice Writer.
The metric correctly checks 'page_break_before_conclusion' instead of the generic 'has_page_break', matching the updated expected.rules.
Negative-control resistance is sound: the original document has no page breaks, so page_break_before_conclusion=False fails the expected=True rule correctly.
The postconfig saves the file (Ctrl+S) before evaluation, ensuring the getter reads the latest document state.

Fix 5 was applied: previously problematic nested helper functions (para_has_page_break_before, prev_para_ends_with_page_break) were inlined into the main getter body, resolving the rule-validation naming-convention errors.

Minor: the backward walk through empty paragraphs before the Conclusion paragraph does not strictly limit how far back it can go, which could theoretically produce false positives if a page break exists far back with only empty paragraphs in between — unlikely in a normal document.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: To eliminate the false-positive edge case in the backward walk, consider adding a maximum lookback limit (e.g., stop after visiting at most 2 consecutive empty paragraphs) so a distant page break elsewhere in the document is not credited as being 'before Conclusion'.
The 'has_page_break' field returned by the getter is computed but not used by the metric; it can be removed to simplify the getter.
